claim: Twitch disclosed that it paid out more than $1 billion to streamers in 2022 while approximately 7 million streamers went live on the platform each month, implying a mean of roughly $143 per monthly-active streamer per year.
stance_target: The typical creator on a major platform earns a trivial amount, and even the arithmetic mean falls far below any living wage
scope_conditions: Both figures are Twitch self-disclosures with no methodology; 'streamer' is undefined (presumably an account that went live at least once in a month); the two figures may not cover identical populations or periods; the mean is inflated relative to the median by extreme top-tail concentration
quoted_support: According to Twitch, it paid out more than $1 billion to streamers in 2022. ... On a monthly basis, some 7 million streamers go live on Twitch, the company says.
region: Twitch global; no country breakdown disclosed

claim: Twitch's Partner Plus program, effective 1 October 2023, requires at least 350 recurring paid subscriptions maintained for three consecutive months to qualify for a 70/30 revenue split, capped at the first $100,000 per 12 months after which the rate reverts to 50%.
stance_target: Platform-set monetisation thresholds define a measurable and demanding boundary for commercially serious creator status
scope_conditions: Twitch Partners only (already an elite subset); net subscription revenue only, not ads or Bits; threshold resets each calendar year
quoted_support: To qualify, Twitch Partners must maintain a sub count of at least 350 recurring paid subscriptions for three consecutive months. ... Once a streamer earns $100,000 through Partner Plus, the revenue share will return to standard rate of 50% for most partners.

claim: Clearing Twitch's elevated Partner Plus threshold of 350 subscriptions yields roughly $1,200 per month in gross subscription revenue, which is below a US living wage before tax and before production costs.
stance_target: Even platform-designated 'successful' creator tiers do not by themselves constitute a living wage
scope_conditions: Derived figure: 350 subs x $4.99 x 70% = ~$1,223/month, assuming all tier-1 subs and excluding ads, Bits, sponsorships; the underlying threshold and rate are directly stated by Twitch
quoted_support: Twitch Partners must maintain a sub count of at least 350 recurring paid subscriptions for three consecutive months.

claim: Twitch reports 31 million average daily visitors and 2.5 million average concurrent viewers against 7 million monthly streamers, giving a ratio of roughly one live streamer for every 4.4 daily visitors.
stance_target: Creator supply has grown far faster than attention supply, structurally capping per-creator revenue
scope_conditions: Twitch self-disclosed 2023 figures; daily visitors and monthly streamers are different time bases, so the ratio is indicative rather than exact
quoted_support: The Amazon-owned platform says it has more than 31 million average daily visitors (and that at any given moment an average of 2.5 million people are watching livestreams). On a monthly basis, some 7 million streamers go live on Twitch, the company says.
